question: Should ClawHub adopt a 40-character skill display-name maximum while grandfathering unchanged existing over-limit hosted and GitHub-backed titles?
rationale: Current behavior defines no maximum, and both the numeric limit and legacy-title treatment change publisher and catalog behavior in ways that source inspection cannot determine.

options.title: Adopt 40 characters with grandfathering
options.body: Apply the shared limit to new or renamed titles while preserving unchanged existing hosted and GitHub-backed names.

options.title: Choose a different maximum
options.body: Keep the shared cross-path validation design but revise the numeric limit and focused tests before landing it.

options.title: Use presentation-only constraints
options.body: Retain unrestricted stored names and constrain catalog rendering or publisher guidance instead of rejecting input.

recommendation.title: Adopt 40 characters with grandfathering
recommendation.body: Apply the shared limit to new or renamed titles while preserving unchanged existing hosted and GitHub-backed names.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest merged-history connection to the backend publish, GitHub sync, and compatibility-sensitive validation paths involved in this decision.
